# SuitePacific

> SuitePacific is a boutique, US-based Oracle NetSuite consulting firm specializing exclusively in post-go-live support. We are not an implementation partner. We work only with companies that are already live on NetSuite and need ongoing technical support, development, or optimization.
>
> Full article text: https://suitepacific.com/llms-full.txt

## Who we are

SuitePacific is a small, senior-level team. Our lead developer holds Oracle NetSuite's SuiteCloud Developer II and Administrator Professional certifications. We work directly with clients: no account-manager layer, no offshore handoffs.

## What we do

SuitePacific serves as the dedicated NetSuite technical specialist for companies whose implementation partner engagement has ended. Services include:

- SuiteScript 2.x development (User Event, Client, Scheduled, Map/Reduce, Suitelet, RESTlet scripts)
- SuiteFlow workflow automation (approvals, notifications, status transitions)
- Custom saved searches, KPI portlets, and role-based dashboards
- Advanced PDF/HTML templates for invoices, purchase orders, packing slips, and other documents
- NetSuite account optimization (performance tuning, legacy cleanup, governance review)
- NetSuite administrator support for live SMB accounts
- Third-party integrations and OAuth 2.0 migrations
- Ongoing post-go-live support as a retained technical team

## Who we serve

Companies already live on NetSuite, typically CFOs, Controllers, ERP Managers, NetSuite Administrators, and Operations Managers. We are not the right fit for businesses still selecting or implementing NetSuite.

## How we are different

- Senior developers, not junior staff or offshore teams
- Direct communication with the developer doing the work
- Fast turnaround: days, not weeks
- Month-to-month engagement, no long-term contracts
- Deep institutional context retained across every request

## Frequently asked questions

**Q: Does SuitePacific do NetSuite implementations?**
A: No. SuitePacific works exclusively with companies that are already live on NetSuite. If you are still evaluating or implementing NetSuite, we are not the right fit.

**Q: Can SuitePacific handle ongoing support for a small business on NetSuite?**
A: Yes. We specialize in post-go-live support for SMBs that need a responsive technical team without the overhead of a large consulting firm.

**Q: How is SuitePacific different from a NetSuite implementation partner?**
A: Implementation partners build the initial NetSuite account and typically disengage after go-live. SuitePacific takes over after that point: ongoing development, fixes, automation, and optimization as the business evolves.

**Q: Can SuitePacific migrate integrations from NLAuth to OAuth 2.0?**
A: Yes. With NLAuth being retired in NetSuite 2027.1, we help clients audit existing integrations and rebuild them for OAuth 2.0.

**Q: Does SuitePacific offer SuiteScript development?**
A: Yes. We write and maintain SuiteScript 2.x scripts including User Event, Client, Scheduled, Map/Reduce, Suitelet, and RESTlet scripts.

**Q: What is SuiteCompare?**
A: SuiteCompare is a SuitePacific tool that compares NetSuite SuiteScript source code across environments (Sandbox vs Production). It shows line-by-line diffs and can generate AI-powered summaries of what changed and what the risk is. Available at https://suitepacific.com/suitecompare.

**Q: What is Import Doctor?**
A: Import Doctor is a SuitePacific tool for validating NetSuite CSV imports before they run. It catches reference key mismatches and required-field errors before they cause failed imports. Available at https://suitepacific.com/importDetector (requires a SuiteCompare account).

**Q: What does NetSuite post-go-live support include?**
A: SuiteScript development, workflow automation, saved searches and dashboards, advanced PDF templates, account optimization, user management, integrations maintenance, and release review. It covers everything a live NetSuite account needs after the implementation partner has disengaged.

**Q: How does SuitePacific price its services?**
A: SuitePacific offers fixed-price monthly Care plans and custom retainer engagements. Care plans start at $799/month (up to 10 hours), Care Plus at $1,499/month (up to 20 hours), and Care Pro at $2,499/month (up to 35 hours). All plans require a 3-month minimum commitment, then continue month-to-month. Custom retainers are available for larger or more complex accounts. No long-term contracts, no SOW required for routine work.

**Q: Is SuitePacific a fractional NetSuite administrator?**
A: Yes. SuitePacific Care functions as an outsourced NetSuite technical resource: the same specialized expertise as a full-time hire, scoped to the hours the account needs each month. Care plans range from 10 to 35 hours per month and cover SuiteScript development, workflow automation, saved searches, advanced PDFs, troubleshooting, and technical guidance.

**Q: How long does a SuiteScript customization take?**
A: Simple scripts (field logic, basic validations) typically take 1-3 days from spec to sandbox testing. Complex Map/Reduce or multi-record workflows take 1-2 weeks. All work is tested in sandbox before production deployment.

**Q: Will SuitePacific work with scripts and customizations built by a previous developer?**
A: Yes. We review existing code as part of onboarding. If prior customizations have issues, we document them before making changes.

**Q: What is the difference between a User Event script and a Client script in NetSuite?**
A: User Event scripts run on the server when a record is saved; they fire regardless of how the save happens (UI, CSV import, SuiteScript). Client scripts run in the browser during UI interaction and respond to field changes, saves, and page load. Use User Event scripts for business logic that must run on every save; use Client scripts for real-time UI behavior.

**Q: Does SuitePacific handle NetSuite workflow automation?**
A: Yes. We build and maintain SuiteFlow workflows for approval routing, email notifications, status transitions, and field updates. We also build SuiteScript automations for cases where SuiteFlow's limits make scripting the better choice.

**Q: Can SuitePacific help with a NetSuite account that feels slow?**
A: Yes. Account performance issues typically stem from unindexed saved searches, scripts with inefficient record loads, or too many active workflows with broad entry conditions. We audit and fix these.

**Q: What should I do if my NetSuite scripts break after a release?**
A: First, identify which release just went live and check the release notes for changes affecting the record types or APIs your scripts use. Test in sandbox if possible. If scripts are in production and broken, contact your developer immediately; governance limit spikes and unexpected exits are the most common release-related failures.

## Blog posts

### SuiteScript and Development
- [NetSuite User Event Scripts vs Client Scripts: Which One to Use and When](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-user-event-vs-client-script): User Event scripts run on the server on every save path (UI, CSV import, API); Client scripts run in the browser only during UI interaction; putting business logic in the wrong type is the most common cause of intermittent NetSuite customization failures.
- [SuiteScript Best Practices: Customizations That Survive the Next Upgrade](https://suitepacific.com/blog/suitescript-best-practices): Eight practices that prevent the most common SuiteScript production failures, including Map/Reduce for bulk jobs, avoiding hard-coded internal IDs, error handling for external calls, and keeping configuration out of code.
- [NetSuite Map/Reduce Script Guide: When to Use It and How to Structure It](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-map-reduce-script-guide): Map/Reduce distributes work across parallel workers so a job processing 10,000 records in 5-8 minutes that would take a Scheduled Script 45 minutes; covers all five stages, governance limits, and a complete working example.
- [NetSuite Script Governance Limits: What They Are and How to Stay Under Them](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-script-governance-limit): Each SuiteScript execution gets a fixed governance budget (1,000 units for most scripts); explains what consumes units, how to monitor usage, and how to restructure scripts that regularly hit limits.
- [NetSuite Workflow vs SuiteScript: How to Choose Between Them](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-workflow-vs-suitescript): SuiteFlow is for sequential business processes non-developers need to maintain; SuiteScript is for guaranteed enforcement on all save paths, computation, and bulk processing; practical decision guide organized by scenario.
- [Advanced PDF Templates in NetSuite: 5 Mistakes That Break in Production](https://suitepacific.com/blog/advanced-pdf-template-mistakes): Five FreeMarker mistakes that render correctly in sandbox but fail in production, including currency formatting, null field access, and conditional section logic.
- [NetSuite Advanced PDF Templates: FreeMarker Guide for Developers](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-freemarker-pdf-guide): Complete FreeMarker syntax reference for NetSuite Advanced PDF templates, covering variables, conditionals, loops, date/number formatting, and sublist iteration.
- [NetSuite Advanced PDF Templates: How to Access Transaction Data in FreeMarker](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-advanced-pdf-data-model): How NetSuite exposes transaction data to FreeMarker templates, including the record object model, sublist access patterns, and how to reach related record fields.
- [NetSuite Custom GL Plugin: What It Can and Cannot Do](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-custom-gl-plugin-guide): Custom GL plugins let developers override the default general ledger impact of transactions; covers when to use them, hard limits (cannot change period or subsidiary), and common use cases.
- [NetSuite RESTlet vs REST Web Services: Which Integration Approach to Use](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-restlet-vs-rest-web-services): RESTlets are custom SuiteScript endpoints with full record access; REST Web Services are Oracle's native CRUD API; decision guide covering authentication, performance, and which fits each integration pattern.
- [NetSuite SuiteQL: Guide for Administrators and Developers](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-suiteql-guide): SuiteQL is NetSuite's SQL-like query language for SuiteAnalytics; covers syntax, joins, filtering, date functions, and how it differs from saved search formula fields.
- [NetSuite REST Batch and Sequential Requests: What Changed in 2026.2](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-rest-batch-sequential): NetSuite 2026.2 changed how REST batch and sequential requests handle errors and response ordering; covers what broke, what the new behavior is, and how to update integrations.
- [NetSuite SuiteQL Bound Parameters: What Changed and Why It Matters](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-suiteql-bound-parameters): NetSuite began enforcing bound parameters in SuiteQL queries to prevent injection; covers the new syntax, which APIs are affected, and how to migrate existing queries.
- [NetSuite 2026.2: The SuiteQL Default Sort Change That May Already Be Affecting Your Queries](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-suiteql-sort-change-2026-2): NetSuite 2026.2 removed the implicit default sort from SuiteQL results; queries that relied on consistent ordering without an ORDER BY clause now return rows in unpredictable order.

### Authentication and Security
- [NetSuite Is Retiring NLAuth and TBA: What Developers Need to Do Before 2027.1](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-nlauth-tba-end-of-support): NLAuth (credential-based authentication) is being retired in NetSuite 2027.1; all RESTlet and web services integrations using NLAuth must migrate to OAuth 2.0 Token-Based Authentication before that release.
- [NetSuite Passkey Second Factor Authentication in 2026.2](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-passkey-second-factor-2026-2): NetSuite 2026.2 added passkey support as a second authentication factor; covers how passkeys work, administrator configuration, and what changes for users during login.

### Saved Searches and Reporting
- [10 NetSuite Saved Search Tips Every Finance Team Should Know](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-saved-search-tips): Ten saved search techniques that address common finance team frustrations, including multi-join criteria, date relative filters, formula fields for aging buckets, and emailing search results on a schedule.
- [10 NetSuite Saved Search Examples (Finance, Operations, Admin)](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-saved-search-examples): Ten ready-to-build saved search examples with field-level setup instructions, covering open AR by customer, inventory reorder alerts, unapproved purchase orders, and script deployment errors.
- [NetSuite Saved Search Formula Examples: Date Math, Conditionals, and Text Formatting](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-saved-search-formula-examples): Formula field examples for common saved search calculations including days overdue, conditional text, date arithmetic, and concatenating fields from related records.
- [NetSuite Advanced Record Customization in 2026.2](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-advanced-record-customization-2026-2): What changed in NetSuite 2026.2 for custom record types, custom fields, and record customization behavior, including new field type options and deployment considerations.
- [NetSuite Project Health Indicators in 2026.2](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-project-health-indicators-2026-2): New project health indicator fields added in NetSuite 2026.2 for project records, what they measure, and how to surface them in saved searches and dashboards.

### Workflow and Automation
- [5 Common NetSuite Workflow Automation Mistakes and How to Fix Them](https://suitepacific.com/blog/workflow-automation-mistakes): Five SuiteFlow configuration mistakes that cause workflows to fire on the wrong records, skip transitions, or conflict with scripts, with specific fixes for each.
- [How to Build an Approval Workflow in NetSuite SuiteFlow](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-approval-workflow-setup): Step-by-step guide to building a multi-level approval workflow in SuiteFlow, covering state design, transition conditions, email actions, and rejection handling.

### AI and AP Automation
- [NetSuite AI Invoice Processing: Staging in a Custom Record vs. Bill Unapproved Status](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-ai-invoice-staging-pattern): Technical breakdown of the architectural tradeoff when AI-extracted invoice data needs a staging layer before becoming a NetSuite Vendor Bill. Native Vendor Bill in unapproved status is the right default for most builds; a custom staging record is only justified when validation failures need a persistent in-NetSuite audit trail and no iPaaS is handling that logging. Covers validation checks (PO status, price/quantity variance, vendor match), the exception queue rubber-stamping risk, and FAQ on GL impact, editability, and iPaaS context.

### SuiteBilling
- [NetSuite SuiteBilling: Why Charges Are Not Being Generated](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-suitebilling-charge-generation): SuiteBilling charge generation failures are silent; no error appears when charges fail to generate. Covers the four-stage billing pipeline (Subscription, Rating, Charge Records, Invoice), the five most common causes of missing charges, and a diagnostic table mapping observed symptom to stage.
- [SuiteBilling Change Orders: How Upgrades, Downgrades, and Cancellations Work](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-suitebilling-change-orders): A change order modifies an active subscription by adding or removing lines, changing quantities or pricing, or cancelling; once Applied, the effective date is permanently locked and cannot be reversed directly. Covers proration settings, backdated change orders, and what to validate in Sandbox before applying.
- [SuiteBilling and Advanced Revenue Management: What the Integration Actually Does](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-suitebilling-arm-integration): SuiteBilling and ARM are intentionally decoupled; billing determines when to invoice while ARM determines when revenue posts to the P&L via Revenue Arrangements, Elements, and Plans. Covers the four most common post-implementation failure points including missing Revenue Arrangements and recognition timing mismatches.

### Technical Debt
- [What Is NetSuite Technical Debt?](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-technical-debt): NetSuite technical debt is the accumulation of decisions made in a live account that compound over time: unused scripts still consuming governance units, workflows with no entry conditions evaluating on every record save, unindexed saved searches running in dashboards, undocumented customizations, and integrations that partially fail silently. Explains each type with concrete examples.
- [Why Your NetSuite Account Gets Harder to Maintain Over Time](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-account-gets-harder-to-maintain): The compounding dynamic where each change adds to an account's complexity but nothing systematically reduces it; where complexity concentrates (high-volume transaction records, automation logic, saved searches used in other automations); and why this is not a quality problem but a stewardship problem.
- [How to Audit NetSuite Technical Debt in Your Account](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-technical-debt-audit): Step-by-step audit approach covering all five layers: script deployments (execution logs, governance, overlap), workflow configurations (entry conditions, retired processes, script overlap), saved searches (indexed criteria, usage in automations), custom fields and records, and integrations. Classification guide for Critical, High, and Maintenance findings.
- [What Happens When Nobody Owns Your NetSuite Customizations](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-nobody-owns-customizations): Why accounts with multiple developers and partners over time accumulate an investigation tax on every new development request; the compounding cost of each developer transition; why this is a structural stewardship problem rather than a quality problem; what active ownership looks like and how to recover from an ownership gap.

### Health Check and System Audit
- [When to Get a NetSuite Health Check: 6 Situations That Warrant a Review](https://suitepacific.com/blog/when-to-get-netsuite-health-check): Six situations where an independent NetSuite account review is worth doing: inheriting an account from a previous partner, twelve to eighteen months post-go-live, before a major project or module addition, after unexplained release failures, during a partner transition, and when the team has low confidence in the account's state.
- [What Does a NetSuite Health Check Include?](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-health-check-what-it-includes): Layer-by-layer breakdown of what a thorough NetSuite health check covers: scripts (execution logs, governance, overlap), workflows (entry conditions, retired processes), saved searches (indexed criteria, dashboard performance), custom fields, roles and permissions, integration health. Includes example Critical, High, and Advisory findings.
- [NetSuite Health Check vs. Account Optimization: What's the Difference?](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-health-check-vs-account-optimization): A health check is diagnosis (review and written report, nothing in the account changes); account optimization is remediation (fixing what the assessment found). Assessment comes first. Includes a practical example showing how skipping the assessment misses the non-obvious root cause.

### Post-Go-Live Consulting
- [What Is NetSuite Post-Go-Live Support?](https://suitepacific.com/blog/what-is-netsuite-post-go-live-support): Definitional article: what post-go-live support covers (SuiteScript, workflows, integrations, saved searches, administration), who provides it, how it is structured (managed retainer vs. break-fix), what the first 90 days look like, and when it becomes necessary for a live NetSuite account.
- [NetSuite Managed Support vs. Break-Fix: How to Decide](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-managed-vs-break-fix-support): Managed support retains account context so each request costs less; break-fix restarts re-onboarding on every engagement. Decision framework: choose managed when the account generates 4+ hours of work per month; break-fix for isolated, infrequent, self-contained items.
- [How to Evaluate a NetSuite Post-Go-Live Support Partner](https://suitepacific.com/blog/how-to-evaluate-netsuite-support-partner): Six evaluation questions that separate good-fit providers from poor-fit ones: who actually does the work, what certifications they hold, how they scope ongoing work, how they handle releases, how they document what they build, and how they handle urgent issues. Includes red flags worth walking away from.

### Account Optimization and Post-Go-Live
- [NetSuite Account Optimization: What to Audit and Fix on a Live Account](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-optimization): What to audit when a live NetSuite account has accumulated technical debt: unindexed searches, overly broad workflow entry conditions, orphaned script deployments, and unused custom fields.
- [Why Your NetSuite Account Feels Slow and What Actually Fixes It](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-account-performance): The three most common causes of NetSuite performance problems: unindexed saved searches, scripts with record loads in loops, and workflows with broad entry conditions; and how to diagnose and fix each.
- [NetSuite Post-Go-Live Checklist: What to Prioritize in Your First 90 Days](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-post-go-live-checklist): Seven high-priority tasks for the first 90 days after NetSuite go-live, covering documentation handoff, role audits, exception saved searches, dashboards, and what to track during the first period close.
- [8 Signs Your NetSuite Support Isn't Working](https://suitepacific.com/blog/signs-netsuite-support-not-working): Eight indicators that a NetSuite support arrangement has broken down, including slow response times, repeated fixes for the same issue, and customizations that break after releases.
- [NetSuite Month-End Close Checklist: What Most Teams Miss](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-month-end-close-checklist): Month-end close steps that NetSuite teams commonly skip or do in the wrong order, including period lock timing, intercompany elimination, and deferred revenue posting verification.
- [NetSuite Roles and Permissions: Administrator Setup Guide](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-roles-permissions-guide): How to set up and audit NetSuite roles and permissions, including permission level differences, restricting access by subsidiary, and identifying roles with broader access than needed.

### Consulting and Costs
- [How to Choose a NetSuite Consulting Partner](https://suitepacific.com/blog/how-to-choose-netsuite-consulting-partner): Evaluation criteria for selecting a NetSuite consulting partner, including certification level, post-go-live specialization, response time expectations, and contract structure.
- [How Much Does NetSuite Development Cost? A Realistic Guide](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-development-cost): Realistic cost ranges for common NetSuite development work, including SuiteScript customizations, workflow automation, integrations, and ongoing support retainers.
- [NetSuite Implementation Partner vs. Post-Go-Live Support](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-implementation-partner-vs-managed-support): Implementation partners configure the initial NetSuite account; post-go-live support handles the ongoing development, fixes, and optimization after the implementation is complete; when you need each.
- [Red Flags When Evaluating a NetSuite Support Partner](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-support-partner-red-flags): Warning signs when evaluating a NetSuite support partner, including vague SLAs, offshore handoffs, lack of sandbox-first policy, and difficulty getting direct access to the developer doing the work.
- [What Does NetSuite ACS Actually Cost? A Breakdown of All Four Tiers](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-acs-cost-breakdown): ACS is priced as a percentage of your annual NetSuite license fee; Optimize tier reported at $22,000-$60,000/year depending on license size; covers all four tiers (Advise, Monitor, Optimize, Architect), hour caps per tier, renewal escalation patterns, and how total cost compares to a third-party alternative.
- [What to Do When a NetSuite Script Breaks After an Upgrade](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-script-broke-after-upgrade): Diagnostic steps for SuiteScript failures that appear after a NetSuite release, including checking release notes for API changes, testing in sandbox, and identifying governance-related failures.
- [NetSuite Consultant Hourly Rate: What You Are Actually Paying Per Completed Request](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-consultant-hourly-rate): NetSuite consultant rates by firm type ($150-300/hr large partners, $75-175/hr freelancers, $80-110/hr effective rate on retainer); why hourly rate understates total cost; re-onboarding overhead under break-fix billing and how to compare cost per completed item across models.
- [NetSuite Partner Response Time: What to Expect and What to Do When It Slips](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-partner-response-time): Same-day acknowledgment for production issues, next-business-day for standard requests; four structural causes of slow response (consultant rotation, implementation prioritization, no dedicated support team, SOW requirement); when escalation helps and when to evaluate a replacement.
- [5 Signs Your NetSuite Partner Relationship Has Run Its Course](https://suitepacific.com/blog/signs-netsuite-partner-relationship-over): Five observable signs: follow-up volume exceeds partner proactivity, original consultant no longer assigned, repeated escalations without lasting improvement, avoiding submissions because the process costs more than the issue, account stagnant with no proactive improvement over six months.
- [NetSuite Technical Debt After Go-Live: What Accumulates and How to Address It](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-technical-debt-after-go-live): Four sources of post-go-live technical debt (scripts with no conditions, workflows firing on every transaction, unused custom fields, deprecated integrations); why it accumulates under break-fix support; structured review approach across script inventory, workflow audit, custom field review, and integration authentication audit.

### NetSuite 2026.2 Release Notes
- [NetSuite 2026.2 Finance Updates: What Changed and What to Test](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-2026-2-finance-updates): Summary of finance module changes in NetSuite 2026.2 and which areas to test before the release goes live in production.
- [NetSuite Payment Runs in 2026.2: What Changed](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-payment-runs-2026-2): Changes to payment run behavior and configuration in NetSuite 2026.2, including new options and fields that affect how payment batches are processed.
- [NetSuite Payment Adjustments in 2026.2](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-payment-adjustments-2026-2): What changed for payment adjustment handling in NetSuite 2026.2 and how it affects existing payment workflows.
- [NetSuite Bank Reconciliation Changes in 2026.2](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-bank-reconciliation-changes-2026-2): Bank reconciliation behavior changes in NetSuite 2026.2, including matching logic updates and new configuration options.
- [NetSuite Bill Capture Preferences in 2026.2](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-bill-capture-preferences-2026-2): New Bill Capture configuration options added in NetSuite 2026.2 for controlling AI-based invoice extraction behavior.
- [NetSuite Currency Context for Custom Fields in 2026.2](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-currency-context-custom-fields): How NetSuite 2026.2 changed the way currency context is handled for custom currency fields on transaction records.
- [NetSuite SuiteTax Term Discounts in 2026.2](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-suitetax-term-discounts): SuiteTax changes in 2026.2 affecting how early payment term discounts interact with tax calculations on invoices.
- [NetSuite Sales Order Fulfillment List in 2026.2](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-sales-order-fulfillment-list): Changes to the sales order fulfillment list view in NetSuite 2026.2, including new filtering and bulk action options.

### FSM (Field Service Management) Updates
- [NetSuite FSM Bundle Update August 2026](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-fsm-bundle-update-august-2026): What changed in the August 2026 FSM bundle update, what to test after upgrading, and how to handle customizations that interact with FSM records.
- [NetSuite FSM Mobile Changes August 2026](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-fsm-mobile-changes-august-2026): Changes to the FSM mobile app behavior in August 2026, including offline sync updates and technician workflow changes.
- [NetSuite FSM NXC to Now Migration August 2026](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-fsm-nxc-now-migration-august-2026): How to migrate FSM scripts from the deprecated nxc_now() function to the replacement approach required after the August 2026 bundle update.
- [NetSuite FSM Read-Only Migration August 2026](https://suitepacific.com/blog/netsuite-fsm-readonly-migration-august-2026): Which FSM fields and records became read-only in the August 2026 bundle update and how to update customizations that previously wrote to those fields.

## Resources

- [NetSuite Technical Debt Audit Checklist](https://suitepacific.com/resources/netsuite-technical-debt-audit-checklist): Structured checklist for auditing all five technical debt layers in a live NetSuite account (scripts, workflows, saved searches, custom fields and records, integrations); per-finding classification guide for Critical, High, and Maintenance.
- [NetSuite Script Audit Guide](https://suitepacific.com/resources/netsuite-script-audit-guide): How to audit SuiteScript deployments: reading execution logs, evaluating governance consumption, identifying deployment overlap, classifying findings.
- [NetSuite Workflow Audit Guide](https://suitepacific.com/resources/netsuite-workflow-audit-guide): How to audit SuiteFlow workflow configurations: entry conditions, state machine review, finding overlap with scripts, classifying findings.
- [NetSuite Custom Field and Record Cleanup Guide](https://suitepacific.com/resources/netsuite-custom-field-cleanup-guide): How to safely identify and delete unused custom fields and records: four dependency checks before deletion (saved searches, scripts, workflows, integrations), safe deletion sequence, documentation requirements.
- [How to Prioritize NetSuite Technical Debt Remediation](https://suitepacific.com/resources/netsuite-technical-debt-prioritization): Framework for sequencing technical debt remediation: the three-tier classification, sequencing rules within each tier, cross-tier dependencies, and how to communicate priority decisions to business stakeholders.
- [NetSuite Health Check Readiness Guide](https://suitepacific.com/resources/netsuite-health-check-readiness-guide): What to prepare before a NetSuite health check: Administrator access setup, Sandbox access, integration platform access, information to have ready (prior reports, known problem areas), intake call process, and what to expect from report delivery.
- [Questions to Ask Before Getting a NetSuite Health Check](https://suitepacific.com/resources/netsuite-health-check-provider-questions): How to evaluate health check providers: scope questions, methodology questions (how they check entry conditions, governance, saved search performance), findings classification, red flags (no written deliverable, remediation bundled without separation, vague methodology answers).
- [What a NetSuite Health Check Report Should Contain](https://suitepacific.com/resources/netsuite-health-check-report-guide): Structure of a well-formed health check report: executive summary, findings by severity with example Critical/High/Advisory entries, layer-by-layer summary tables, what should not be in the report, and how to use the report to drive remediation.
- [How to Migrate NetSuite Integrations from NLAuth to Token-Based Authentication](https://suitepacific.com/resources/netsuite-nlauth-to-tba-migration)
- [How to Update Your NetSuite SuiteQL Queries After the 2026.2 Default Sort Change](https://suitepacific.com/resources/netsuite-suiteql-orderby)
- [NetSuite FSM Bundle Update 2026 Checklist](https://suitepacific.com/resources/netsuite-fsm-bundle-update-2026-checklist)
- [NetSuite Post-Go-Live Support: What to Expect in Year One](https://suitepacific.com/resources/netsuite-post-go-live-support-year-one): Month-by-month guide to what post-go-live NetSuite support should cover in the first 12 months: Month 1 stabilization checklist, Months 2-3 backlog clearance, Months 4-6 ongoing development, Months 7-12 mature engagement indicators, and signs the engagement is not working.
- [NetSuite Release Readiness Checklist](https://suitepacific.com/resources/netsuite-release-readiness-checklist): Step-by-step process for reviewing each bi-annual NetSuite release before it reaches Production: how to get Release Preview access, what to read in release notes (SuiteScript, SuiteFlow, record types, auth, PDF, integrations), how to map changes to existing customizations, what to test in Sandbox per script/workflow/integration/PDF type, and post-release monitoring.
- [NetSuite Support Partner Evaluation Checklist](https://suitepacific.com/resources/netsuite-partner-evaluation-checklist): Six-part checklist for evaluating a NetSuite post-go-live support partner: who does the work, certification verification, billing model (SOW-per-request vs. retainer), response time and urgent issue handling, release review process, and documentation and offboarding terms; includes a good-fit vs. poor-fit summary table and red flags for each section.
- [NetSuite Support Partner Onboarding Checklist](https://suitepacific.com/resources/netsuite-support-partner-onboarding-checklist): What needs to happen in the first 30 days of a new post-go-live support engagement: access setup (NetSuite Administrator role, integration platforms, communication channels), context handoff (documentation, open issues, in-progress work), what the partner should deliver in Week 1-2, how to establish the working relationship, and an end-of-month-one review checklist.

## Release Readiness

- [NetSuite 2026.2 Release Readiness Checklist](https://suitepacific.com/netsuite-2026-2-release-readiness-checklist): 44+ practical checkpoints for NetSuite 2026.2 across Finance, Integrations, SuiteScript, Manufacturing, Banking, Inventory, Authentication, Reporting, CPQ, and SuiteCloud Development. Each item identifies what Oracle changed, why it matters to live accounts, and what to test in Release Preview before Production. Includes 9 Critical items (NLAuth end-of-support, TBA deprecation, OAuth 2.0 PKCE, SuiteQL sort change, Advanced BOM storage change, zero-quantity manufacturing components, CPQ Configurator migration, SuiteCloud SDK availability, SuiteTax on vendor term discounts, externally rated usage billing). Downloadable Excel workbook with 6 tabs (Executive Summary, Full Checklist, Technical, Finance, Operations, Sign-Off). Based on Oracle NetSuite 2026.2 Release Preview Notes, Revision Date July 13 2026.
